t:
(a) In General.—Activities authorized by part A of title IV of the Social Security Act, and by sections 510, 1108(b), and 1925 of such Act, shall continue through June 30, 2005, in the manner authorized for fiscal year 2004, notwithstanding section 1902(e)(1)(A) of such Act, and out of any money in the Treasury of the United States not otherwise appropriated, there are hereby appropriated such sums as may be necessary for such purpose. Grants and payments may be made pursuant to this authority through the third quarter of fiscal year 2005 at the level provided for such activities through the third quarter of fiscal year 2004. 
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 403(a)(3)(H)(ii) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 603(a)(3)(H)(ii)) is amended by striking “March 31” and inserting “June 30”.

fable.w: This section only extends existing Social Security Act programs through June 30, 2005, appropriates the funds for them, and makes a conforming date amendment. The tempting reading is that grants and payments to states involve outside parties, but receiving grant funding is not consultation or participation in a federal decision. The section requires no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.
fable.s: Grants and payments may be made pursuant to this authority through the third quarter of fiscal year 2005 at the level provided for such activities through the third quarter of fiscal year 2004.

opus.w: This section extends existing Social Security Act programs through June 30, 2005, provides the money for them, and changes a date from "March 31" to "June 30." It mentions grants and payments, which may go to states, but grants and benefits are excluded from the definition of participation. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
opus.s: Grants and payments may be made pursuant to this authority through the third quarter of fiscal year 2005 at the level provided for such activities through the third quarter of fiscal year 2004.
opus.b: 1. The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section talks about grants and payments that go to states, which are outside the federal government. That reading fails: under the definition, grants and benefits are not participation, and nothing here has the government consult anyone before deciding something. The section just extends TANF and related programs, funds them, and changes a date.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations and the continuation of grant programs. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside the federal government; it is purely a funding mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: Grants and payments may be made pursuant to this authority through the third quarter of fiscal year 2005 at the level provided for such activities through the third quarter of fiscal year 2004.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because grants are made to states or local entities, this involves coordination with outside parties. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. This section is purely an appropriation and continuation of existing grant authority, not a requirement for consultation or public input.
